claims.claim: **iGAS carries significant morbidity and mortality**, and household contacts of a case are at increased risk of secondary iGAS.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Invasive group A streptococcal infections: management of household contacts' (Last updated May 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Invasive_group_A_streptococcal_infections__management_of_household_contacts/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **iGAS = GAS isolated from a normally sterile site:** bacteraemia/septicaemia · streptococcal toxic shock syndrome · necrotising fasciitis · pneumonia and empyema · meningitis · osteomyelitis or septic arthritis · retropharyngeal abscess.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Invasive group A streptococcal infections: management of household contacts' (Last updated May 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Invasive_group_A_streptococcal_infections__management_of_household_contacts/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cellulitis, scarlet fever and pharyngitis are not invasive disease.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Invasive group A streptococcal infections: management of household contacts' (Last updated May 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Invasive_group_A_streptococcal_infections__management_of_household_contacts/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Household contact** = over 24 hours spent in the case's house, from 7 days before symptom onset until 24 hours after effective antibiotics began.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Invasive group A streptococcal infections: management of household contacts' (Last updated May 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Invasive_group_A_streptococcal_infections__management_of_household_contacts/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Secondary cases usually occur within a month, mostly in the first 7 days.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Invasive group A streptococcal infections: management of household contacts' (Last updated May 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Invasive_group_A_streptococcal_infections__management_of_household_contacts/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Inform household contacts about iGAS features and give chemoprophylaxis as soon as possible.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Invasive group A streptococcal infections: management of household contacts' (Last updated May 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Invasive_group_A_streptococcal_infections__management_of_household_contacts/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The evidence for chemoprophylaxis is limited** — some experts and guidelines recommend it, but it has not been studied extensively.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Invasive group A streptococcal infections: management of household contacts' (Last updated May 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Invasive_group_A_streptococcal_infections__management_of_household_contacts/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Whether or not prophylaxis is given, educate every household contact** on their raised risk and the signs needing prompt review: fever · sore throat · severe headache · severe muscle aches · vomiting or diarrhoea · cellulitis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Invasive group A streptococcal infections: management of household contacts' (Last updated May 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Invasive_group_A_streptococcal_infections__management_of_household_contacts/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not throat-swab asymptomatic close contacts** to assess carriage — it does not help.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Invasive group A streptococcal infections: management of household contacts' (Last updated May 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Invasive_group_A_streptococcal_infections__management_of_household_contacts/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic household contacts need not isolate or restrict activities.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Invasive group A streptococcal infections: management of household contacts' (Last updated May 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Invasive_group_A_streptococcal_infections__management_of_household_contacts/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric or infectious diseases team** for non-household close contacts, or if adherence to chemoprophylaxis is a concern.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Invasive group A streptococcal infections: management of household contacts' (Last updated May 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Invasive_group_A_streptococcal_infections__management_of_household_contacts/, retrieved 2026-09-23
